facts.text: Off-road braking differs from road braking both in magnitude and in the factors that dominate braking performance.
facts.quote: Off-road braking differs from road braking in magnitude and in what dominates it.

facts.text: New South Wales guidance specifies an off-road in-service minimum deceleration of 0.60 m/s².
facts.quote: 0.60 m/s² in-service minimum in New South Wales guidance

facts.text: The US MSHA table specifies off-road deceleration of about 2.94 m/s².
facts.quote: about 2.94 m/s² in the US MSHA table

facts.text: Car automatic emergency braking has a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s².
facts.quote: a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² for car automatic emergency braking

facts.text: Latency is a first-order contributor to stopping distance at work-site speeds: at 5 to 15 km/h, the delay term can account for half or more of stopping distance.
facts.quote: Latency is a first-order term at work-site speeds: at 5 to 15 km/h the delay term can be half or more of the stopping distance.

facts.text: Grade and payload change available off-road deceleration by the same order as the deceleration itself.
facts.quote: Grade and payload shift available deceleration by the same order as the deceleration itself

facts.text: The recommended core model for off-road stopping distance is a calibrated point-mass model incorporating measured latency, brake build-up lag, and worst-case deceleration dependent on grade, payload and surface.
facts.quote: A calibrated point-mass model with measured latency, a brake build-up lag and a worst-case deceleration that depends on grade, payload and surface is the right core model for stopping distance

facts.text: Higher-fidelity off-road braking models pay off only for brake hydraulics, articulated and high-center-of-gravity stability, hydrostatic drives and soft ground.
facts.quote: higher fidelity pays off only for brake hydraulics, articulated and high-center-of-gravity stability, hydrostatic drives and soft ground.

facts.text: A fixed time-to-collision threshold is a weak primary brake-intervention trigger at work-site speeds.
facts.quote: A fixed time-to-collision threshold is a weak primary trigger at work-site speeds

facts.text: Published consensus and the ISO 21815-3 structure favor a stopping-distance and risk-zone brake-intervention formulation, with time to collision used as one input.
facts.quote: the published consensus and the ISO 21815-3 structure favor a stopping-distance and risk-zone formulation with time to collision as one input.

facts.text: The brake-intervention ladder is warn, advise, slow, stop and inhibit motion from standstill.
facts.quote: The intervention ladder is warn, advise, slow, stop and inhibit motion from standstill.

facts.text: No universal maximum automatic deceleration exists for earth-moving machines.
facts.quote: No universal maximum automatic deceleration exists for earth-moving machines

facts.text: The published position for earth-moving machines is to command the minimum of the deceleration needed to avoid collision and the deceleration allowed by stability, brake capacity and payload, with a jerk limit.
facts.quote: the published position is to command the minimum of what is needed to avoid the collision and what stability, brake capacity and payload allow, with a jerk limit

facts.text: Simulation-tuned brake-intervention thresholds have been checked against field results on-road.
facts.quote: Simulation-tuned thresholds have been checked against field results on the road, never off-road.

facts.text: Simulation-tuned brake-intervention thresholds have never been checked against off-road field results; no published off-road case quantitatively compares simulation-tuned thresholds with field results.
facts.quote: Simulation-tuned thresholds have been checked against field results on the road, never off-road. No published off-road case compares simulation-tuned thresholds with field results quantitatively.

facts.text: The lack of a published quantitative off-road comparison between simulation-tuned brake-intervention thresholds and field results is the program's main technical risk.
facts.quote: No published off-road case compares simulation-tuned thresholds with field results quantitatively. This gap is the program's main technical risk
